A story from Europe’s edge

Why carry
Europe’s flag
into the smoke?

In Tbilisi and Kyiv, Europe is not a bureaucracy. It is a direction. Romania has known that direction for two centuries.

Tbilisi · 2024

Follow the idea ↓
Paris1789

Before Europe was an institution, it was an argument.

An old word changed its meaning.

A subject belonged to a ruler. A citizen belonged to a political community—and could ask by what right power ruled.

liberté nation droit citoyen

The French Revolution did not invent liberty, and it did not keep faith with all its promises. It also produced terror, war and empire.

But it made a radical claim audible across a continent: legitimacy could come from citizens, not dynasty; law could bind the state; a people could imagine itself as a nation.

The language would travel farther than the Revolution.

At Europe’s other edgelate 18th century

A country that did not yet exist

The idea arrived before the borders.

Moldavia and Wallachia lived under Ottoman suzerainty. Transylvania lay in the Habsburg world. Russia was moving toward the Black Sea and the Danube.

There was no Romanian state to defend. First, there had to be a Romanian political imagination.

Ромын becomes român

The nation begins as a sentence

Scholars of the Transylvanian School made Latin ancestry a cultural and political argument. The gradual turn from Cyrillic to Latin script placed Romanian beside French and Italian—kinships that could be read on the page.

French supplied more than fashionable words. It helped name a modern public world: society, liberty, constitution, nation.

Paris1848

The school of a generation

They came west to learn how a future sounded.

Bălcescu Rosetti Brătianu Ghica

In Paris, young Moldavians and Wallachians entered the lectures, salons and arguments of post-revolutionary France. They read Michelet and Quinet. They met one another as members of a nation not yet on the map.

When Paris rose again in February 1848, the shock crossed Europe. In June, at Islaz, a Romanian programme demanded political equality, responsible government, wider representation and emancipation.

The French vocabulary had become a Romanian project.

Wallachia1848

Translation, not imitation

The revolution lost. The programme survived.

Foreign intervention ended the revolutions in the principalities. But defeat scattered their authors into exile, where they turned revolution into diplomacy.

Paris became an amplifier for the Romanian cause. After the Crimean War, the Congress of Paris placed the principalities inside a European settlement. In 1859, Moldavia and Wallachia chose the same prince. Union became a fact before every empire had agreed to the word.

1848programme
1856European opening
1859union
1864civil law

Ideas became institutions: schools, codes, ministries, boulevards. Bucharest looked toward Paris not because imitation was enough, but because a young state needed forms strong enough to endure.

Bucharest1866

A Latin nation. A German prince.

To become more securely itself, Romania chose a foreign dynasty.

Carol of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen brought dynastic legitimacy, diplomatic weight and distance from local faction. Under him, the fragile union gained independence and became a kingdom.

The apparent contradiction was the design: French political culture, German statecraft, Romanian national ambition. Western anchoring was never a matter of purity. It was a way to make sovereignty durable.

East of Europe1812—present

The counterforce

Every westward choice was made beneath an eastward pressure.

This is not a myth of eternal enemies. Geography is not destiny, cultures are not regimes, and no people is condemned to repeat its rulers. But power has direction—and repeated expansion creates a history prudent nations cannot pretend not to know.

1812

Bessarabia

Russia annexed the eastern half of Moldavia through a treaty with the Ottoman Empire. Moldavia was not at the table.

1878

An ally’s price

Romania fought beside Russia and won independence—then was compelled to cede southern Bessarabia to its ally.

1940

The ultimatum

The Soviet Union seized Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina. Annexation was followed by arrests, deportations, resettlement and Russification.

After 1944, Romania itself was forced into the Soviet sphere. The state remained on the map while much of its sovereignty moved elsewhere.

Empire changes a border.
Then it tries to change memory.

Europe’s unfinished bordernow

The idea comes home

For Romania, Europe was never merely somewhere else.

After communism, joining NATO and the European Union answered an old question with new institutions: how can a country on the border remain free without remaining alone?

Ukraine and Georgia ask versions of that question today. Their European flags do not erase national identity. They insist that a nation may choose its laws, its alliances and its future without permission from an empire.

A message from the border

From the centre,
Europe can look like an inheritance.

From the edge, it looks like a promise.

France gave Romania a language in which to imagine political freedom. Germany helped give the young state a form. Europe, at its best, gave national cultures a way to live together without conquest.

Romania’s story is a tribute to that inheritance—and a warning that inheritance survives only when someone chooses to defend it.

The flag in the smoke is where the story begins again.
